answer: To resist sybils, every agent must lock a bond whose funding ancestry is published on-ledger. The protocol then clusters those graphs: keys that share one funding river are merged and sit on a single ledge of weight equal to the smallest lock, not the sum of the copies. A nebula of sockpuppets paid from one treasury therefore buys almost no extra influence. An attacker who wants n independent votes must acquire n uncorrelated capital streams and lock each for a full epoch, paying the market cost of those assets plus the time the capital cannot be used elsewhere.
